title: Automated Terraform CI: VPC Health Guard, Migration Checks, and Policy Fix Hints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a hardened CI pipeline for Private/VPC Terraform deployments that enforces policy-as-code, validates migration safety, runs post-apply health probes, and surfaces automated remediation hints. The pipeline must run fast enough for developer feedback (pre-apply) and be conservative for production applies (canary + gated rollout). Primary drivers: reduce outages from infra changes, catch drift and incompatible upgrades early, and make policy violations actionable with suggested fixes.
implementation_notes: Add a pre-commit and CI lint stage using tflint + terraform fmt + checkov (baseline ruleset used by infra team).

Introduce a gated plan stage that runs in an isolated 'preapply' workspace: generates a full plan json, runs Conftest (rego) policies over the plan, and produces a human-readable report alongside failing rules and suggested fixes.
If Conftest flags only non-blocking warnings, attach suggestions and mark MR as 'policy-warnings' for PM/ops review. Blockers should fail the pipeline.

Implement an opt-in automated fixer for low-risk issues: run terraform-validate fixes (formatting, minor tag fixes) in a branch and open a PR with the changes. This runs only when the author opts in via MR label 'auto-fix-iac'.
Plan artifacts must be stored in artifact storage for auditability and to feed the post-apply healthcheck job.
Canary apply: for production VPC changes, the pipeline must support staged applies (canary to a subset of subnets or a non-prod mirror), smoke tests, and automatic rollback on health failures.

Post-apply health probes: run a suite of network sanity checks (route table connectivity, security group reachability, NAT gateway egress tests) and a lightweight infra-prober that validates the expected Terraform outputs (IPs, subnets, route propagation).
Integrate with Console alerting: failed policies or health checks must create a ticket in the infra incident board and emit a metric to the SLO dashboard.
Performance consideration: Conftest runs on plan JSON; for large plans use sharding by module path to keep feedback time under 90s for typical PRs.
Fallbacks: if the plan artifact is unavailable, pipeline should fail with clear troubleshooting steps.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline defined in repo 'infra/terraform' with stages: lint -> plan -> policy-check -> manual-approval (for prod) -> apply -> post-healthcheck
Conftest policies run on plan JSON and produce a summarized report uploaded to the MR with pass/fail, failing rules, and suggested remediations.
Automated low-risk fixes can be created as MR when 'auto-fix-iac' label is applied; maintainers can opt out.
Post-apply healthcheck job runs within 10 minutes of apply completion and returns pass/fail and structured probe logs.
Pipeline creates an artifact record pointing to plan.json and healthcheck logs in the deployments audit dashboard.
SLO: median pre-apply feedback time for a single-module change should be < 90 seconds (depends on plan size sharding).
qa_steps: Create a sandbox branch that modifies a non-prod VPC module and open MR. Ensure lint and plan stages pass and policy report is attached.
Add an MR that intentionally violates a Conftest rule (for example, missing required tags). Verify the pipeline fails and MR comment includes suggested fix text from policy rule metadata.
Apply a change to a canary subnet and verify post-apply health probes detect connectivity and expected Terraform outputs. Verify rollback trigger when probe fails.
Label an MR with 'auto-fix-iac' on a simple formatting issue and confirm an automated fix MR is created with the proposed changes.
Simulate artifact store outage: ensure pipeline fails early with actionable instructions and logging for SRE team.
